in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week

conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to ask you some questions about your child or children.

**First question: How old is your child?**

This helps determine their eligibility category:
- Children under 16 generally qualify automatically (with some conditions)
- Children aged 16-19 may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children aged 20 or over are not eligible

Please tell me your child's age. If you have multiple children you're asking about, we can go through them one at a time.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Thank you for that information. Alex is 6 years old, so he's under 16.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news - since Alex is only 6 years old, he's well under the age limit. Now I need to check a few more conditions.

**Next question: Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week (or not in paid work)?**

At 6 years old, I expect the answer is that he's not working at all, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility check.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all. He's only 6!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You're absolutely right - of course he's not working! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in their own right?**

In other words, is Alex receiving Employment and Support Allowance (ESA) or Universal Credit in his own name? 

Again, at 6 years old, this is unlikely, but I need to check all the eligibility conditions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the checks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Next question: Is Alex in any type of apprenticeship?**

Since he's only 6, I'm confident he's not, but this is another required check. Certain types of apprenticeships can affect eligibility for older children.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship. He's just 6 years old!

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Absolutely right - I appreciate your patience with these questions! Let me move forward.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we're moving on to questions about **you** as the claimant. 

**Next question: Do you meet the UK residency requirements for Child Benefit?**

You can qualify if **ANY** of the following applies to you:

1. **You normally live in the UK**, or
2. You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or
3. You have pre-settled status and are working (earning above the National Insurance threshold for 3 months), or
4. You have pre-settled status and are actively seeking work (up to 91 days), or
5. You have pre-settled status with sufficient resources to support yourself, or
6. You have pre-settled status and are studying with sufficient resources, or
7. You have pre-settled status as a family member of an EEA/Swiss national with right to reside, or
8. You're living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Do any of these apply to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply to me. I don't live in the UK - I live abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I see. Since you don't meet any of the UK residency requirements, let me navigate to the outcome for this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Result: **INELIGIBLE**

I'm sorry, but based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit** for Alex.

### Why you're ineligible:

While Alex meets all the child-specific requirements (he's 6 years old, not working, not receiving benefits, and not in an apprenticeship), **you do not meet the UK residency requirements**.

To claim Child Benefit, you must:
- Normally live in the UK, **OR**
- Have settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme (with certain qualifying conditions), **OR**
- Be living abroad as a Crown servant or in certain qualifying countries

Since you live abroad and don't meet any of these special circumstances, you cannot claim Child Benefit.

### What you could consider:

- If your circumstances change and you move to the UK to live normally, you could apply at that time
- If you have settled or pre-settled status that you haven't mentioned, that might change your eligibility
- If you're a Crown servant working abroad, that could also affect your eligibility

If you have any questions about this decision or your specific circumstances, you may want to contact the Child Benefit Office directly for personalized advice.

**Reference:** [GOV.UK Child Benefit Eligibility](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/eligibility)
